You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The data fits early 2010. Unemployment is 9.7%, the fed funds rate is about 0.16%, and core CPI is 1.33% and falling. Equity 12-month returns are +50%, which implies a window from March 2009 to early 2010. VIX is 17.13, and the 10-year yield is 3.88%.

For the month, US large-cap equity is up 4.7% over 1 month and the drawdown is about -0.3%, so the index is at a high. The 10-year yield of 3.88% fits either December 2009 (about 3.84%) or February 2010 (about 3.61%). The 12-month return of 50% points to a window ending between February and April 2010. Core CPI at 1.33% YoY fits roughly February 2010 (about 1.3%).

April 2010 is more consistent with most of the other figures:
- The S&P 500 was up about 1.5% in April 2010, not 4.7%.
- March 2010 was up about 6%.
- The 10-year yield was 3.83% in March and 3.85% at the end of April.
- Unemployment was 9.7% in both February and March 2010, and 9.9% in April.
- Payrolls averaged -57k over 3 months, which fits the period ending February 2010.
- CPI YoY was 2.1% in February, 2.3% in March, and 2.2% in April. Core was 1.3% in both February and March, and 0.9% in April.

Balancing the equity return against the rest, I judge that the snapshot is most likely March 2010. The 1-month equity gain of 4.7% roughly fits March (about 6%), and the 12-month return of 50% fits March 2010 (about 49.8%). The 10-year yield of 3.88% fits March's 3.83-3.88%. The 1-month decline of 1.2% in 7-10y Treasuries also fits March.

The 3-month payroll average of -57k fits March 2010 as well, since payrolls were -14k in Feb and +ish in March, and later revised.
